narr: Rain and a few storms traversed the area on the night of February 27th, then activity began to increase the morning of the 28th as a cold front slowly approached from the west. Strong to severe storms initially developed out ahead of a convective line during the early morning hours of the 28th. The front edge of the line pushed into Southeast Ohio and Northeastern Kentucky shortly before daybreak and then continued east across West Virginia into the early afternoon on the 28th.||In Kentucky, the strongest winds and most robust storm activity occurred along the leading edge of this line. One inch hail was reported in Carter County, and shortly after a wind gust of 61 miles per hour was measured in Boyd County. In addition to storms, one to one and a half inches of rain fell over soils that were already saturated from rain the previous day. Flash flooding occurred along some of the smaller creeks and streams during the morning, then Tygarts Creek exceeded its bankfull level and led to flooded roadways in the vicinity of the Olive Hill gauge. Rain exited to the east by the afternoon of the 28th and flooding came to an end that same evening.
ev: Dry Fork exceeded its banks and caused flooding at the junction of Dry Fork Road and Aden Road.
Near Olive Hill, Perry Branch exceeded its banks and caused flooding along State Route 2078. Within the next hour, Perry Branch also caused flooding along Hall Lane.
